lower.thumbnailCopy: Hover over an app to see up to six window previews. A minimized window may show the app icon if a thumbnail is unavailable.
lower.switcherCopy: Browse up to 20 windows reported by Accessibility, including minimized ones. Choosing a window on another Space can switch Spaces.
lower.quotaCopy: See your 5-hour and weekly quotas, when they reset and whether you’ll run out at your current pace. Set alerts before you hit a limit.
lower.diskCopy: Check free and purgeable space from the tray, alongside Wi-Fi and battery. Review caches and Git worktrees before removing them.
lower.themeCopy: Pick a theme for the bar, panels and previews. Adjust the bar’s transparency from 0 to 80% while icons and text stay opaque.
lower.featureIntro: Preview windows, check your Mac and keep track of your coding quotas from the bar.
lower.permissionHint: Toggle a permission to see what changes.
lower.flowUsage: Usage is on by default. Cala checks quotas with Anthropic and OpenAI using your existing sessions.
lower.usageOff: Turn off Usage in Settings → Usage.
lower.flowReports: Sentry receives reports you send. Crash reports ask first by default. You can opt into automatic sending.
lower.reportsOff: To disable crash reports, choose Never in Settings → Advanced.
lower.flowJoin: Your browser or video app opens the link from your calendar event when you choose Join.
lower.joinOff: Hide the Join button in the taskbar.
lower.flowDownload: GitHub serves the release when you download the DMG or run the installer.
lower.downloadOff: You can build Cala from source instead.
lower.accountDetail: Use the bar without signing up. Quotas and calendars use accounts you already have.
lower.signDetail: Cala ships without a Developer ID signature because Apple’s program costs US$99 a year. macOS asks once when you open the DMG version.
lower.checksumDetail: The Terminal installer compares the DMG’s checksum with the one published for that release before installing.
lower.privacyIntro: Cala has no analytics. Here’s what stays on your Mac and when it connects to a service.
lower.usageTech: Cala reads local quota data when available. For remote reads, it queries Anthropic using the Claude Code access token. Codex uses its local app-server or the ChatGPT endpoint with its existing token and account ID. Claude Code may send a short “ok” prompt to Haiku to renew an expired token, which uses a little quota.
lower.reportRedaction: Cala redacts the home folder, user name, Mac name and email addresses in diagnostics. If sending is unavailable in your build, you can copy the report and paste it into an issue.
lower.footerLine: A free taskbar for macOS 14 and later.

specs: Free · macOS 14+ · Apple silicon and Intel
mobileLead: Cala is for Mac. Open this page on your Mac or copy the link.
demoHint: Hover over an app or click a tray icon.
demoTouch: Tap an app or a tray icon.
featuresTitle: Your windows and controls, close at hand.
switcherText: Choose from up to 20 windows, including minimized ones. Hover over an app for up to six previews. A minimized window may show its app icon when a thumbnail is unavailable.
trayText: Check Wi-Fi, battery and free disk space from the tray. Use More for controls you need less often.
performanceText: See what uses the most CPU and memory, and why a restart might help.
eventsText: Open the clock for upcoming events. When a call is about to start, join from the bar.
installIntro: The same universal app runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs with macOS 14 or later.
terminalInstruction: Open Terminal with Spotlight (⌘ + Space), paste this command and press Return.
terminalResult: It downloads the latest release, checks its SHA-256 checksum, installs Cala in Applications and opens it. This method skips the one-time macOS prompt. Run it again to update and keep your settings.
dmgStep2: Open the DMG and drag Cala into Applications.
dmgStep3: Allow Cala to open once. After that it opens normally.
newStep1: Double-click Cala in Applications. When you see the verification message, click Done.
newStep2: In System Settings, open Privacy & Security and scroll to the bottom.
newStep3: Click Open Anyway next to the Cala notice and enter your password.
newStep4: Open Cala again and choose Open Anyway.
sonoma: In Applications, right-click Cala, choose Open, then confirm with Open again.
welcome: Follow Cala’s four short welcome steps. You can skip any of them.
permissionsLead: Cala explains each request and takes you to the right place in System Settings. You can skip any permission and still use the rest of the app.
permissionsLater: To grant them later, right-click an empty part of the bar and open Settings → Permissions.
accessPurpose: See, focus, minimize and close windows. It also enables Option + Tab.
accessWithout: The bar still opens apps, without window controls.
recordPurpose: Shows window thumbnails. Cala never saves a recording or sends your screen.
calendarPurpose: Shows upcoming events and the Join button.
locationPurpose: macOS needs it to show Wi-Fi network names.
finderPurpose: Counts and empties the Trash, and restarts your Mac on request.
finderWithout: Those actions are unavailable in Cala.
notificationsPurpose: Shows Claude or Codex quota alerts.
permissionNote: For Accessibility and Screen Recording, turn on Cala in the list macOS opens using Touch ID or your password. If macOS offers Quit & Reopen after Screen Recording, accept it.
privacySummary: Cala requires no account and uses no analytics. Window previews and calendar events are processed on your Mac.
privacyDataTitle: What leaves your Mac and when
privacyUsageText: On by default, the indicator uses your existing Claude Code and Codex credentials. It checks Claude’s quota with Anthropic. For Codex it uses the local codex app-server process or contacts OpenAI directly through ChatGPT.
privacyUsageControl: Claude Code can send Haiku a short “ok” prompt to renew an expired token, using a little quota. Turn off the Usage switch in Cala’s Settings → Usage.
privacyReportsText: If reporting is configured, Cala sends reports to Sentry. Before sending, you can review your message, optional email and attachments. In ordinary reports, “Include technical information” controls the detailed diagnostics attachment. Cala still sends your Mac model, macOS version, permission status and some settings when it’s off. A crash report you send manually always includes crash.ips and diagnostics.txt.
privacyCrashText: Cala asks before sending crash reports by default. With automatic sending enabled, Cala sends the .ips file and diagnostics the next time it opens.
privacyActionsText: Join opens the video call link. The Terminal installer downloads Cala from GitHub and verifies the published SHA-256 checksum.
privacySourceText: The source is public. You can read it, inspect the installer and build Cala yourself.
privacySignText: Cala is distributed without an Apple Developer ID signature. The Apple Developer Program costs 99 USD a year. If you use the DMG, macOS asks you to allow Cala to open once.
requirementsA: Cala runs on macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later. The download is universal for Apple silicon and Intel.
updatesA: Run the install command again, or download the new DMG and replace Cala in Applications. Your settings and permissions are kept.
uninstallA: In Cala, go to Settings → Advanced → Uninstall Cala. It restores the Dock and menu bar, removes the login item, deletes Cala’s settings and moves it to the Trash. You can remove its permissions in System Settings → Privacy & Security.
blockQ: Why does macOS block the DMG install?
blockA: Cala is distributed without an Apple Developer ID signature. macOS asks for your approval the first time you open it from Applications.
unlockLink: See the steps for your version of macOS
